title: IS12:: countdown2.c (4.2)

lines.code: Primary objective: practicing simple while loop with countdown control

lines.explanation: Since we may want to run this program with different starting values of the loop counter, it is wise to make this starting value a definable constant

lines.code: int counter = HOW_MANY; /* setting the counter */
lines.explanation: This variable will be used as a loop counter. It is declared as integer and initialized with the definable constant HOW_MANY
The line Start counting will be printed before the loop

At each iteration of the loop, the current value of the counter is checked. If this value is zero (0), the loop will will be skipped, otherwise execution will proceed with the first statement inside the loop.
This statement does two things. It prints the current value of the counter and also decrements the value of counter. Since post-decrement is used here, the value printed is the one before decrement.
This is the first statement after the loop. Here the execusion will resume when checking the expression controlling the loop (counter) we will find that it became zero
